references.text: Describes the actual laying on of hands on the ram during the consecration of Aaron and his sons, which was commanded here in Exodus 29:15.
Gives instructions about laying hands on the head of the burnt offering, the same ritual action described here with the ram.
Describes laying hands on the head of the sacrifice animal for the peace offering, showing the repeated pattern of this ritual act.
Contains instructions about laying hands on the head of the sin offering, illustrating the symbolic transfer of sin to the sacrificial animal.
Describes the second ram (the consecration ram) where Aaron and his sons also lay their hands on the ram's head, as a parallel to this first ram.
The Levites lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, showing that laying on of hands was a central part of consecration rituals.
The book of Hebrews refers to the daily sacrifices that priests had to bring and points to Christ as the final sacrifice that replaces these repeated offerings.
The instruction for the action in Exodus is fulfilled historically in Leviticus with the second ram.
The same laying on of hands ritual is performed on the sin offering bull as part of the same consecration process.
